title: Introduce kernel-level heatmap and cost-flow annotator for invocation traces
author: Arianna Chen
description: Motivation: We need a low-overhead way to surface GPU/kernel-level queuing and contention hotspots correlated to token-level cost and per-stage latency. This PR adds a sampled, lightweight kernel-heatmap export and a cost-flow annotator that stitches stage timing with kernel occupancy to help SREs and runtime engineers diagnose expensive invocation patterns. Design summary: 1) A new kernel heatmap sampler emits compact histograms of kernel queue wait and execution time per-device and per-invocation-phase; sampling is prioritized for requests that exceed a configurable latency or cost threshold. 2) A cost-flow annotator postprocesses traces to attach a per-invocation-stage cost attribution vector (model load, key-value cache miss penalties, kernel stalls, token-generation time) and synthesizes rollup markers used by dashboards. 3) Minimal on-path overhead: sampler uses atomic ring-buffers and amortized aggregation at a local telemetry worker; annotation is done asynchronously by the trace aggregator to avoid adding tail latency. Implementation details: Added a new runtime probe (runtime/probes/kernel_sampler.cc) with export hooks to the observability pipeline, a proto schema (telemetry/protos/kernel_heatmap.proto) and a canonical generator for the annotator (observability/annotators/cost_flow_annotator.go). Also updated the console dashboards (dashboards/infra/kernel-heatmap-panel.json and dashboards/infra/cost-flow-explorer.json) and the SLO playbook (runbooks/kernel-contention.md). Rollout plan: feature gated behind observability.kernel_heatmap flag, disabled by default for existing customers. Canary enabled for internal clusters and a stage behind the rollout gate; follow-on step will enable 0.1% sampling for hosted tier and 1% for dedicated, then iterate. Backfill: included a small backfill job (observability/scripts/backfill_heatmap.py) to index recent traces for correlation testing. Testing: unit tests for sampler ring-buffer and proto serialization, integration test that validates annotations appear on traces end-to-end, and a perf microbenchmark showing <1.3% median p99 increase when sampling at 0.1% on benchmark lab. Migration/rollback: feature flag removal and a short migration script to drop the temporary heatmap index if disabled. Related: ENG-5421 (investigation into GPU contention during long prompts), ties to runbook playbooks introduced in previous telemetry work.

release_notes: Add kernel-level sampled heatmaps and a cost-flow annotator for invocation traces. Feature is behind feature flag observability.kernel_heatmap and disabled by default; initial rollout will be canary then small percentage sampling. Provides new dashboard panels and operator runbook for diagnosing kernel contention and per-stage cost attribution.
notes_for_ops: If enabling at scale, monitor telemetry/sampler_memory and telemetry/heatmap_queue_drops. Backfill job should be run during low traffic. Rolling back requires disabling feature flag and running drop_heatmap_index migration script.
risk_profile: medium: introduces new telemetry exports and storage, but guarded by feature flag. Compatibility shim added to avoid breaking older collectors.
post_merge_tasks: Enable feature flag for internal canary cluster
Run backfill_heatmap.py against last 7 days in staging
Observe telemetry/sampler_memory and adjust sampling thresholds
human_readable_summary: This PR instruments kernel queue/execution hotspots and stitches them into token-stage cost attributions. It adds lightweight sampling in the runtime and asynchronous annotation in the trace pipeline, plus dashboards and runbook. The feature is gated and rolled out gradually to limit overhead and storage growth.
